title: A Real Photo Joins the Model Effects Family | vitalii.no
description:
How extracting the shared timing, camera and check logic behind a played guitar and a folding solid into one kit let a fourth effect — a real photo with a walking camera — get built on top of it.

Showing a real thing in a lesson — an instrument actually being played, a solid folding out of its flat net, a real photo worth exploring — meant building each effect from scratch with its own timing and camera code every time. The pile of near-duplicate logic only grew with every new idea.

I built three model effects as plain Remotion components with real physics: a guitar effect that models actual pitch and loudness as a string is played, a solid-build effect that folds a 3D solid from its 2D net, and an example-series effect that runs a stated rule through a series of worked examples with a think-pause before each solution. All three register in a new model-effects list, kept separate from the night writers' usual effect catalogue since their variety rules don't apply. I then extracted the shared parts these three needed anyway — phases, camera moves, checks, look, plus callout, counter and question-block helpers — into one shared model kit, and used that kit to write a fourth effect: a labelled-picture effect that takes a real photo, map or painting and walks the camera to up to six labelled points instead of drawing a diagram.

Four model effects now exist, backed by three proof cards, with the newest one proving the extracted kit works as a foundation for whatever model comes next.
